The article "Developing and Evaluating a Website as an OER for Faculty Development" addresses the need for effective faculty development (FD) programs in liberal arts institutions. In East Asia, new faculty trained at large research universities often struggle to adapt to the pedagogical requirements of liberal arts education. At the International Christian University (ICU) in Japan, there was an urgent need to support new faculty in understanding liberal arts values, mastering instructional design, and balancing professional responsibilities with well-being.

Using the ADDIE model, researchers developed a web-based FD program consisting of 20 modules categorized into administrative functions (R-Modules), tenure and teaching effectiveness (I-Modules), and liberal arts values and teaching strategies (T-Modules). The website was built using Google Sites and released under a Creative Commons license as an Open Educational Resource (OER).

Evaluation through qualitative and quantitative methods indicated the website is an effective tool. Qualitative analysis showed materials were informative and easy to navigate, though participants requested a Japanese version. Quantitative results showed an average System Usability Scale score of 73, exceeding the global mean of 68. High scores for Perceived Usefulness and Perceived Ease of Use suggest the site is useful and user-friendly. The study concludes that digital OERs can support long-term FD through flexible, self-paced learning and suggests future research include longitudinal studies to track long-term utilization.
